protocolAssumptions.finding: The runner records test failures faithfully but does not distinguish loopback permission errors from product assertion failures. Report them as blocked infrastructure coverage until a permitted rerun; do not count them as passing in the frozen baseline.

The HTTP adapter, authentication, streaming parser, event ordering, cancellation, and final citation plumbing are exercised with synthetic provider frames and fixture credentials. A pass does not establish real provider compliance, deployed FC streaming behavior, proxy buffering, model answer quality, or real source evidence quality.

The fixture extracts production UI functions into a minimal HTML page, while persistence, workspace catalog, context construction, network responses, recommendation normalization, and some event dependencies are mocked. These choices can hide integration defects even when renderer checks pass; no actual hidden integration defect is established by this failure.

Linux without DISPLAY is skipped, while macOS native startup failures reject execFile before its result assertions. The current baseline does not silently pass or skip this failure. A GUI-capable environment is necessary to assess the 43 renderer scenarios.

Existing desktop coverage is an explicit six-file subset rather than the complete desktop test directory. Retrieval replay uses the --fixture lexical model. Passing totals are scoped to selected controlled regression tests and should not be described as an end-to-end production certification.
